title: Indian Restaurant Samudhra Signs 10,000-Square-Foot Lease Near Times Square
excerpt: The Franklin Park, New Jersey-based premium Indian restaurant and lounge will open its first Manhattan location at The Ellery, a luxury mixed-use tower in Hell's Kitchen.
body:
• Samudhra, a premium Indian restaurant from Franklin Park, NJ, has signed a 10,000-square-foot lease at 312 West 43rd Street in Hell's Kitchen
  • The restaurant will be the second location for founder Mangesh Chinthamaneni, a former IT entrepreneur who moved into hospitality
  • Asking rents in the nearby Times Square corridor averaged $1,400 per square foot in Q2 2026, underscoring the high-stakes bet on Indian dining in Midtown Manhattan

Samudhra, a premium Indian restaurant and lounge based in Franklin Park, New Jersey, has signed a 10,000-square-foot lease on the ground level of The Ellery at 312 West 43rd Street in Hell's Kitchen — marking a significant expansion of Indian fine dining into one of Manhattan's most high-profile neighborhoods.

The deal, first reported by the New York Post, places Samudhra in a luxury 33-story mixed-use tower developed by Taconic Partners and National Real Estate Advisors. The space will include a dedicated dining area, bar, and lounge along West 43rd Street, steps from the Times Square theater district.

From IT to Indian Hospitality

Samudhra's founder and CEO, Mangesh Chinthamaneni, is a former IT entrepreneur who pivoted into the restaurant industry. His Franklin Park location, situated at 3391 NJ Route 27, has built a following for its upscale take on Indian cuisine — featuring dishes like Hyderabadi Gosht Dum Biryani, Murgh Bhut Jolokia Tikka, and Panasakaya Pulao (a jackfruit biryani) alongside handcrafted cocktails and a full bar. The restaurant describes itself as a "premium casual" destination that aims to immerse guests in the rich culinary heritage of India.

"The Ellery provides an exceptional setting for our New York City location and gives us the opportunity to introduce our distinctive premium Indian dining and lounge experience to a much broader audience."

— Mangesh Chinthamaneni, Founder & CEO, Samudhra

A High-Rent Bet on Indian Cuisine

The lease terms were not disclosed, but asking rents for prime retail space in the nearby Times Square corridor — along Broadway and Seventh Avenue from 42nd to 47th streets — averaged $1,400 per square foot in the second quarter of 2026, according to CBRE data. For a 10,000-square-foot space, that translates to potential annual rent north of $14 million at full asking price, though restaurant deals in the area typically involve negotiated rates and concessions.

CBRE's Lon Rubackin, Michael Kadosh, and Bevan Cohen represented the landlord, while Brad Schwarz of Lee & Associates handled the deal for the tenant.

Indian Dining's Manhattan Footprint

Samudhra's arrival adds to a growing roster of Indian restaurants staking out ambitious positions in Manhattan. The city has seen a steady evolution from the traditional "Curry Hill" cluster on Lexington Avenue to Indian concepts competing for prime real estate across Midtown and beyond. The Hell's Kitchen location places Samudhra in a neighborhood already dense with international dining options, where it will serve both the Ellery's 330 residents and the area's foot traffic of theatergoers, office workers, and tourists.

"Samudhra brings a premium new dining and social experience that will serve both our residents and the broader neighborhood," George Tsapelas, senior vice president of Taconic Partners, said in a statement. "From the outset, our vision for the Ellery has been to create a dynamic mixed-use destination that contributes to the energy of the area."

The Ellery's Retail Roster

The announcement follows German grocery chain Aldi's 25,000-square-foot lease at the same building roughly a year ago, part of the grocer's broader U.S. rollout. Aldi opened its first Midtown store at the location in June. The Ellery, completed in 2024, filled all 330 of its apartments within 11 months of launching leasing, and offers amenities including a rooftop pool, private gardens, spa areas, fitness center, and coworking spaces.

For Chinthamaneni and Samudhra, the Manhattan expansion represents a test of whether a premium Indian dining concept born in New Jersey's Indian diaspora corridor can translate to a mainstream Midtown audience — and command the rents to match.
